stemMd: A city will increase parking fees to discourage driving downtown. Shopkeepers predict that their sales will fall because fewer customers will arrive by car. Which finding most weakens their prediction?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Parking charges account for a small part of city revenue.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Downtown shops sell a wider range than suburban shops.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Most displaced drivers are expected to visit the same shops by public transport instead.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Some customers currently park outside the charging zone.

explanationMd: The prediction assumes that fewer car arrivals means fewer shopping visits. Substitution to public transport breaks that link while preserving the same customers and purchases. The claim concerns sales, not the number of cars.

distractorRationale.b: Variety alone does not show whether displaced drivers continue buying.
distractorRationale.e: This only describes a subset unaffected by the change, not replacement of lost customers.
distractorRationale.a: The city's revenue mix does not establish shop sales.
distractorRationale.d: Existing discounts do not establish how customers will respond to the fee.
